server.instructions: Look up people and organizations in the Acme staff directory, and manage the support tickets attached to them. Search tools are read-only; ticket tools mutate state.
server.name: acme-directory

tools.description:
Find individual people in the staff directory by name, email, or employee ID.

Use this when the user is looking for a *person*. If they are looking for a company,
team, or other organization, use `search_organizations` instead. Returns one entry per
matching person with their name, email, title, and organization.

limit.description: Maximum number of people to return.
limit.title: Limit

organization_id.description: Restrict results to one organization, e.g. 'org_9f2b'. Omit to search all.
organization_id.title: Organization Id

query.description: Full or partial name, email address, or employee ID to match on.
query.title: Query

tools.name: search_users

tools.description:
Find organizations -- companies, teams, and departments -- by name or email domain.

Use this when the user is looking for a *group*, not a person. To find an individual
inside one of these organizations, use `search_users` instead. Returns one entry per
matching organization with its ID, display name, primary domain, and member count.

include_inactive.description: Include organizations that have been marked inactive.
include_inactive.title: Include Inactive

limit.description: Maximum number of organizations to return.
limit.title: Limit

query.description: Full or partial organization name or email domain to match on, e.g. 'Acme' or 'acme.test'.
query.title: Query

tools.name: search_organizations

tools.description:
Retrieve the full profile for one known person, including contact details and manager.

Use this only when you already have a user ID. If you have a name or email and need to
resolve it to an ID first, call `search_users`.

user_id.description: The user's stable identifier, e.g. 'usr_1a2b'. Get one from `search_users`.
user_id.title: User Id

tools.name: get_user_profile

tools.description:
Open a new support ticket on behalf of a user and return the created ticket.

Use this to file a *new* problem. To change something about a ticket that already
exists, use `update_ticket_status` instead.

body.description: Full description of the problem, including any error messages.
body.title: Body

priority.description: How quickly the ticket needs attention.
priority.title: Priority

requester_id.description: User ID of the person reporting the problem, e.g. 'usr_1a2b'.
requester_id.title: Requester Id

tools.name: create_support_ticket

tools.description:
Move an existing support ticket to a new status, optionally attaching a note.

Use this to progress or resolve a ticket. To permanently remove a ticket from the
active queue, use `archive_ticket` instead.

comment.description: Optional note explaining the status change.
comment.title: Comment

status.description: The status to move the ticket to.
status.title: Status

ticket_id.description: Identifier of the ticket to update, e.g. 'tkt_4c8d'.
ticket_id.title: Ticket Id

tools.name: update_ticket_status

tools.description:
Read the comment thread on one support ticket, oldest first.

Use this to understand a ticket's history before acting on it. This returns only the
conversation; the ticket's own fields come from `create_support_ticket`'s response or
from `update_ticket_status`.

since.description: Only return comments posted on or after this date, as ISO-8601, e.g. '2026-01-31'.
since.title: Since

ticket_id.description: Identifier of the ticket to read.
ticket_id.title: Ticket Id

tools.name: list_ticket_comments

tools.description:
Permanently archive a support ticket, removing it from the active queue.

This cannot be undone from this API -- archived tickets are restorable only by an
administrator. To close a ticket in a way that can be reopened, use
`update_ticket_status` with status 'closed' instead.

reason.description: Why the ticket is being archived, for the audit log.
reason.title: Reason

ticket_id.description: Identifier of the ticket to archive, e.g. 'tkt_4c8d'.
ticket_id.title: Ticket Id

tools.name: archive_ticket

tools.description:
Export one organization's slice of the staff directory as a CSV document, as text.

Use this when the user wants the whole membership as a file or table rather than a
handful of matches; for looking up specific people, `search_users` is cheaper.

fields.description: Columns to include. Defaults to name, email, and title.
fields.title: Fields

organization_id.description: Organization whose members should be exported, e.g. 'org_9f2b'.
organization_id.title: Organization Id

tools.name: export_directory_csv
